target_customer: Independent coffee shops, restaurants and small food brands that use Square point of sale
problem: Independent restaurants lack branded mobile ordering and loyalty apps like Starbucks and rely on third-party delivery marketplaces that own the customer relationship.
business_model: SaaS subscription (from $99 per month per the company site) for white-label branded apps, loyalty and marketing, built on the Square ecosystem
product_category: Restaurant branded app, loyalty and marketing platform (now positioned as an AI operating system)

founders.name: Tomer Molovinsky
founders.background_notes: Podcast description says he came from the military; not opened. YC page lists product roles at OpenTable and Resy.

technical_complexity.rationale: White-label app generation on top of the Square API with loyalty and ordering; standard mobile and integration engineering for a two-person team.

defensibility.rationale: Square integration and merchant data give some lock-in, but white-label ordering apps already had many vendors and depend on Square's platform.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copy was found by Square; Per Diem stayed a Square partner and kept growing, claiming 800 plus brands on the YC page.

market_need_then: Restaurants were paying high marketplace commissions and wanted first-party ordering after the pandemic shift to digital orders; Per Diem's early pitch was Starbucks-level apps for independents. No dated customer-spend figure was opened.

branding.domain_note: Uses tryperdiem.com and per-diem.co, not per-diem.com; per diem also means a travel allowance, which crowds search results.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain pitch around owning the customer relationship and Square-built apps

branding.brand_signature: Rated number one on Square claim and Built for Square positioning

brand_strength.rationale: Search results show the term per diem dominated by travel expense content; the brand itself has little press beyond funding and a Square marketplace presence.

outcome_analysis: Per Diem raised a 2.3 million dollar seed in April 2021 led by Two Sigma Ventures and stayed small with 25 staff while building around Square's marketplace, which gave it distribution. It claims 800 plus brands and 500,000 monthly orders and is still active, with no later priced round found. The risk is dependence on Square, and a shift in 2024 to an AI operating system framing.
notes: The TechCrunch (via Yahoo) and Two Sigma pages could not be opened (redirect, 503, rate limit), so the seed is confirmed by the YC page headline, search summaries of both outlets and CB Insights, not by page text. Total raised conflicts: CB Insights 2.43 million over two rounds; one aggregator says 4.3 million (unverified, not recorded). Revenue growth claim of 24.6 million from a low-authority aggregator is unverified. Competitors: the only competitor search returned current vendor comparison pages (Olo, Toast, ChowNow, Appfront, Punchh) with no sources dated near January 2021, so the list is empty. Founding year varies by source (2017 to 2021); the YC page says 2020. Founder education not stated on sources opened.
